Mixture-of-experts (MoE) routing is a mechanism used in neural networks (particularly in large language models) where the model has multiple "expert" sub-networks, and a routing network decides which experts to use for a given input. The key idea is that instead of having one large network, you have many smaller specialized networks (experts), and a router (typically a small neural network) outputs probabilities/scores for each expert. For each input token, the router computes a gating vector, and the top-k experts (highest scores) are selected. Only those selected experts are activated and their outputs are combined (weighted by the gating values). This other experts are not computed at all - saving computation.
